A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DNAChunker. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial methodological and presentation revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream benchmark results, an H-Net architecture comparison, genomic token-size analyses, and ClinVar mutation-stability measurements.

after.justification: v3 reports DNAChunker benchmark outcomes, including revised Nucleotide Transformer evaluations, and retains original genomic tokenization and ClinVar analyses.

M1.justification: v1's cross-attention dechunking is replaced by boundary-based expansion, bidirectional probability-gated smoothing, and masked residual gating in v3 Section 3.1.3. Table 5 also changes the embedding width from 1024 to 640 and introduces two decoder BiMamba stages. The appendix specifies 30 Transformer blocks instead of eight, although v3's main text still says eight. Cosine-based routing and the MLM/ratio losses remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds Drosophila Enhancers Stark to Genomic Benchmarks and a revised NT evaluation containing additional prediction targets, including H2AFZ, H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K9me3, and H4K20me1 (Table 6). HG38 pretraining, the original NT tasks, existing Genomic tasks, ClinVar categories, and genomic loci remain covered.

E2.justification: The evaluated H-Net comparator disappears. v3 adds MxDNA, PatchDNA, and GENA-LM-Base comparisons in Tables 3 and 6. Within Genomic Benchmarks, CNN and Mamba are removed, while DNABERT-2, NT-v2, GROVER, and Generator-All are added. The original NT Table 1 comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Genomic Benchmarks switches from the Schiff-based five-fold protocol to the Wu-based ten-fold protocol, with different baseline model sizes and revised fine-tuning settings. DNAChunker's reported size changes from 156M to approximately 172M. Section 3.2 changes maximum pretraining length from 2048 to 8192 bp, matching the already-existing v1 appendix value; this does not establish an actual training-length increase. ClinVar content similarity is also redefined in the text, without establishing recomputation.

E4.justification: The direct architecture comparison against H-Net trained with the same MLM scheme and genome (v1 Figure 2) is removed. v3 Section 4.2 instead focuses on DNA-tokenizer comparisons, leaving the revised architectural components without an equivalent direct control. The genomic token-size case studies and ClinVar robustness analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces reporting over three random seeds for revised NT results and changes Genomic Benchmarks aggregation from five to ten folds. It removes the standard errors from the retained ClinVar results (v1 Table 3 versus v3 Table 4). Benchmark reporting otherwise retains the mean-plus-standard-error convention.

E6.justification: v3 adds revised NT results, removes H-Net outcomes, and replaces Genomic Benchmarks results under changed conditions. Original NT estimates also change: DNAChunker's H3 MCC moves from 0.827 to 0.817, while its reported overall MCC remains 0.772; Generator's Splice Site All MCC changes from 0.978 to 0.976. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance changes. v3's revised NT average is inconsistently reported as 0.657 in Table 3 and 0.660 in Table 6.

T1.justification: The decoder's mathematical specification changes from cross-attention to boundary-indexed expansion and bidirectional scans. Section 4.2 revises the content-stability definition from edit distance to one minus normalized edit distance. Routing and loss mathematics remain essentially unchanged; neither version contains a theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The central claims of bidirectional learnable tokenization, biological adaptivity, mutation resilience, and strong downstream performance remain. The introduction revises the parameter-efficiency claim from 156M to 172M parameters against the 1.2B Generator and no longer identifies cross-attention as the architectural contribution.

C2.justification: v1 attributes architectural gains to cross-attention's bidirectionality. v3 develops a different mechanistic account: masked residual gating prevents encoder shortcuts, while smoothing supports bidirectional reconstruction and concentrates contextual modeling in the main network. It adds interpretation concerning adaptive tokenization's splice-site sensitivity and removes the earlier explanation linking modest Mouse Enhancers performance to human-only pretraining.

D1.justification: Architecture and fine-tuning specifications are substantially revised, and v3 newly documents mean chunk positions for RoPE. Generator's task-specific tuning entries and the source-code access/licensing statement disappear. Reproducibility is complicated by new inconsistencies: eight versus 30 Transformer blocks, and a pretraining learning rate of 7e-4 in Appendix C prose versus 5e-4 in Table 7. Removal of the code disclosure does not establish external code unavailability.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused positioning against MxDNA and PatchDNA, discussing conservation-based boundaries, CNN granularity constraints, and splice-site behavior, with new citations to Qiao, Del Vecchio, and Lindsey. It also adds a GELU citation. The general related-work survey and the claimed first application of learnable dynamic chunking to a masked DNA model remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, architectural exposition, tokenizer-analysis narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Architecture receives separate encoder, main-network, and decoder subsections. Appendices are reordered and expanded, the ethics statement becomes an impact section, and the reproducibility statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. The H-Net figure is removed and revised NT tables are added. v1 Figure 3 is split between v3 Figure 2 and appendix Figure 4, retaining all three gene panels; chromosome plots are retained and renumbered. The robustness table is transposed and other tables are substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 adds relevant MxDNA/PatchDNA comparisons and more explicit decoder and mask-handling explanations. However, it removes the H-Net architecture control, ClinVar standard errors, and code-access disclosure, while introducing conflicting architecture and learning-rate specifications and inconsistent revised NT summaries. The added comparative evidence is useful, but these losses and unresolved reporting discrepancies prevent a reliable judgment of the net change in overall paper quality.
